project.name: dream-soft-render
project.summary: A CPU rasterizer for 2D triangle meshes and egui frames. It writes premultiplied RGBA8 into a buffer you own, and the same draw calls give the same bytes on every platform.

notes.summary: First release: the software rasterizer from dream-ini's PortMaster build, with a drawing API of its own and egui as an option.
added: `SoftwareRenderer` and `Frame`: clear, `fill_rect`, `textured_rect` and `mesh`, rasterized immediately into a premultiplied RGBA8 surface.
`create_texture`, `update_texture` and `free_texture`, with handles issued process-wide and never reused.
`Color`, `Vertex`, `Rect`, `ClipRect` and `TextureId`, and one `Error` type for every rejected call.
The `egui` feature: `render_egui`, `RenderFrame`, `RenderOutcome`, and skipping frames whose output did not change.
NEON kernels on AArch64 for translucent spans, textured and glyph rows, gradient rows and coverage scans, held byte for byte to the portable code.
The `draw` and `frame` benchmarks, and golden hashes of four whole frames.
known_issues: A surface wider or taller than 65535 pixels is accepted and draws wrong past pixel 65535. Refused on the default branch.
A texture wider or taller than 65536 texels is accepted and samples the wrong texels. Refused on the default branch.
In `render_egui`, a frame after one whose texture uploads failed part way can be skipped as unchanged and keep the old texels. Fixed on the default branch.
In `render_egui`, textures egui releases in a frame that fails stay in the store and count against the budget. Fixed on the default branch.
In `render_egui`, a mesh with an index past its vertices, or a trailing partial triangle, is skipped instead of failing the frame. Fixed on the default branch.
